clue.text: US sycophant upsetting parish people, about 50 (13, two words)

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters are placed around the numeral that follows
upsetting means the letters of parish people are thrown into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An American toady is upsetting the people of the parish, roughly fifty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' scrambles PARISH PEOPLE and 'about' wraps that jumble round L, the Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: An American idiom for a flatterer, from the schoolchild who polishes an apple for the teacher.

clue.text: Shoot on grouse moor? There's nothing in what's to cook

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the cooking vessel, so one word is put within the other

parts.note: a pot is what you cook food in
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A remark about a shoot on the moors and the empty cooking pot afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a Scots verb: to shoot young grouse, or a young grouse itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means to shoot at young moorfowl, as on a grouse moor.

clue.text: Association for business types in favour of transport

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: A business club that supports public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is that of the clubs for retired professional and business people.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of an international network of clubs for retired professional and business people.

clue.text: Stone I found in hollows

indicators.note: found in means the letter I sits inside the word for hollows

parts.note: a lap is a hollow, as among hills, so hollows are laps

explanation.surface: A gemstone discovered in some hollow places.
explanation.definitionFit: The short name for lapis lazuli, the deep blue semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Knock to indicate needing lift? Tapping noise

indicators.note: in a down clue a lift raises the letters, so the whole run reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to tap is to knock lightly
to tip is to hint at or indicate

explanation.surface: Knocking on a door to show you need a ride, with a tapping sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing lift' turns the whole charade TAPTIP upside down in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduplicated imitative word for a light rapid beat, like a pattering heart.

clue.text: Rock plant for rearing at home

indicators.note: rearing means rising up, so in a down light the word for for is read upwards

parts.note: pro means for
in means at home

explanation.surface: A plant on a rockery being raised at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' turns PRO upwards to ORP.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant name of orpine, a stonecrop that grows on rocks and walls.

clue.text: Strip of wood I held in middle? Jock's averse

indicators.note: held in middle means the I is clasped at the centre of the wood strip

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood

explanation.surface: Someone holding a slat of wood in the middle, though reluctant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jock' is crossword shorthand for a Scot: the answer is the Scots form of loath.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots spelling of the adjective loath, meaning reluctant or unwilling.

clue.text: Tinware in its material, hot

indicators.note: in means the tinware word goes inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: tinware is made of tin, chemical symbol Sn
tole is lacquered or painted tinware

explanation.surface: Tin goods kept in their own metal, and very warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' is slang for stolen goods, not a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods recently taken by theft and risky to handle.

clue.text: Elevation of rank by the sound of it once promised in Scotland

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for elevation is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: height is elevation, as in a high rank or eminence

explanation.surface: A rise in status, apparently, that was pledged to a Scot long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an archaic and Scots past participle of hight, meaning promised or named.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic past participle, still Scots, meaning vowed or pledged.

clue.text: Charm with minor switch, English copy

indicators.note: a minor switch is a small swap, here two letters of the charm trading places

parts.note: an amulet is a charm worn against evil

explanation.surface: A lucky charm with a small switch fitted, copied in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor switch' swaps the A and E of AMULET to give EMULAT, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to imitate or copy someone, usually aiming to equal them.

clue.text: Lake-shore mineral artist crated?

annotationWithheld.why: Lake-shore mineral artist crated? (5): BO(RA)X, where 'crated' must both supply BOX and signal putting RA inside it, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Knick-knacks I caught in two bits of underwear, see

indicators.note: in means I and the cricket letter are held inside the first piece of underwear

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear, and there are two of them
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a bra is an item of underwear, and there are two of them
see sounds like cee, the name of the letter C

explanation.surface: Ornaments with me trapped inside two underwear items, look.
explanation.walkthrough: The first BRA swallows I and C; the second BRA follows, then C.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornaments and curios of little value, a collection of trinkets.

clue.text: Loss of honour in Athens alas includes distinguished citizen thereof? Not on

indicators.note: includes means the sigh word goes around the shortened name

parts.note: ay is an old exclamation meaning alas

indicators.note: Not on means the letters ON are dropped from the name

parts.note: Timon of Athens, Shakespeare's misanthrope, was a noted citizen of that city

explanation.surface: In Athens, alas, even a notable citizen could lose his civic honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thereof' points back to Athens, so the citizen is Shakespeare's Timon; 'Not on' trims his name before it goes inside the sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Athens this was public disgrace, the loss of civic rights and standing.

clue.text: Old gold coin to cheer buckaroo, not the first

parts.note: to yell is to cheer loudly

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a buckaroo is a cowboy

explanation.surface: An old gold coin used to applaud a cowhand.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a gold coin such as a guinea, from its colour.

clue.text: Scottish husky that has work breaking up wild riot

indicators.note: breaking up means the work word splits the rearranged letters apart
wild means the letters of riot run loose into a new order

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hoarse Scot whose work disrupts a violent riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles RIOT to ROIT, which OP breaks into RO and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Here husky means hoarse in voice, and this is the Scots word for it.

clue.text: Devout prankster in Amazonian craft?

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, devout
a rogue is a mischievous prankster

explanation.surface: A religious joker aboard a boat on the Amazon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' is a boat, not a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout canoe used on South American rivers such as the Amazon.

clue.text: Pomeranian makes drooling noise by the sound of it

indicators.text: noise by the sound of it
indicators.note: noise by the sound of it says the word is heard spoken, matching another spelling

parts.note: drooling, one spits

explanation.surface: A small dog that slobbers noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: A Pomeranian is one breed of the spitz family, so the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pomeranian is a small breed of spitz, the family of pointy-eared dogs.

clue.text: Carp from the States I found among a lot of herrings

indicators.note: found among means the following letters go inside the herring measure

parts.note: a cran is a measure of fresh herrings
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A fish from America discovered in a large haul of herrings.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran is a measure of herrings, about 37.5 gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: A European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: One travels via Amtrak, arrival affected, velocity becoming constant

indicators.note: affected means the letters are altered and rearranged
becoming means one letter turns into another

parts.note: V is the symbol for velocity
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A traveller on the American rail network whose arrival is disrupted by a speed change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' changes the V of ARRIVAL to C, and 'affected' rearranges ARRICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled railway carriage, the sort of vehicle running on Amtrak lines.

clue.text: Rainy borders of Hungary and elsewhere

indicators.note: borders of means the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: et al. is short for Latin et alibi, and elsewhere

explanation.surface: Wet weather on the edges of Hungary and other places.
explanation.walkthrough: Et al. usually means 'and others' but also abbreviates et alibi, 'and elsewhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical adjective meaning relating to rainfall.

clue.text: Stoup's content? Namely 'overflowing', about to go fast (9, two words)

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, namely

indicators.note: about means the excess word goes around the speed word

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive or overflowing
to spin along is to go fast

explanation.surface: A remark about a vessel's contents spilling over and about to rush off.
explanation.walkthrough: A stoup is a drinking vessel; the old Scots pint measure was about three English pints.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Scottish liquid measure, a fitting quantity for a stoup or flagon.

clue.text: Stiff rule in wood

indicators.note: in means the rule letter goes inside the word for wood

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

explanation.surface: A rule laid down in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' is slang for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff is slang for a dead body.

clue.text: Home for cats? Some copper Siamese

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A copper-coloured Siamese cat wondering where its kind came from.
explanation.definitionFit: The country gives its name to the Persian, a long-haired breed of cat.

clue.text: Chemical compound, form of nitre containing electric field strength

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters wrap around the symbol
form of means a new arrangement of the letters of nitre

parts.note: E is the symbol for electric field strength

explanation.surface: A chemist describing a compound made from nitre in an electric field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges NITRE to TRINE, and 'containing' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An organic hydrocarbon with three double bonds in its molecule.

clue.text: Like heavy type whenever included, of two kinds

indicators.note: included means the condition word sits inside the type word

parts.note: bold type is heavy type
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, I stay in'

explanation.surface: A printer's note about type that is heavy and of two sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Twofold or double, existing in two forms.

clue.text: Liberal food's passed round in spread

indicators.note: passed round means the food word goes around the party letter

parts.note: fare is food
L stands for Liberal; the reversed run across these words is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A Liberal's food handed round at a buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a meal, matching the food; it is the verb to widen.
explanation.definitionFit: To flare is to widen out, as a skirt or trouser leg does.

clue.text: I'll be included by fellows in self-administered massages

indicators.note: be included by means the letter goes inside the word for fellows

parts.note: dons are college fellows
the I of I'll is the letter used

explanation.surface: Someone joining college fellows at self-massage sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: Do-in is a Japanese form of self-massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Do-in is a Japanese technique of massaging oneself, a form of self-shiatsu.

clue.text: Sprinkle all over set scattered in beer?

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the drink word

parts.note: a brew is a beer

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of set are strewn in new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a scattered set belongs in a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestrew is to strew things over a surface, to cover by scattering.

clue.text: Harrow fern thicket

definitions.meaning: a heavy harrow for breaking clods

explanation.surface: A list of farm gear and rough growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Three separate senses of one word: a heavy farm harrow, the coarse fern bracken, and a dense thicket of brushwood.

clue.text: Drink a lot round Spain in tropical headgear

indicators.note: round means the drinking word goes around the country letter

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Drinking heavily around Spain in a sun hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A light pith helmet worn against the sun in hot countries.

clue.text: What may be articulated, right inside parrot

indicators.note: inside means the right letter goes into the bird name

parts.note: a lory is a brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A talking parrot with the right word inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' sounds like speech, which a parrot suits; it means jointed, as an articulated truck.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulated truck has a jointed cab and trailer, a large goods vehicle.

clue.text: Mild expletive exemplified by commercial

parts.note: e.g. means for example
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A mild oath used as an example in an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned mild oath, a softened form of 'by God'.

clue.text: Lack of gas? A vehicle running short, awful pain

indicators.note: running short means the vehicle word loses its last letter

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: awful means the letters of pain are rearranged badly

explanation.surface: A car running out of fuel causes terrible pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' is carbon dioxide in the blood, not petrol; 'awful' rearranges PAIN to PNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical condition in which the blood has too little carbon dioxide.

clue.text: A skin condition like this is plugged by a pin

indicators.note: is plugged by means the second part fills the inside of the first

parts.note: so means like this, in this way
a peg is a pin

explanation.surface: A skin complaint like this one treated by sticking in a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Scots name for ringworm or a scaly skin disease.

clue.text: Take as a precaution (one might assume) what may run along river?

indicators.note: one might assume hints that the clue reads take 'in case', so the letter goes into the precaution word

parts.note: in case means as a precaution, giving case
R is short for recipe, take, in prescriptions

explanation.surface: Advice to take something just in case, about land along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: As a precaution is 'in case': read 'Take in case' as R inside CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots for low fertile land beside a river, so it runs along the river.

clue.text: Abjure former race forever

parts.note: ren is an old form of run, a race
ay or aye means forever

explanation.surface: Giving up an old race for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are archaic forms: REN for run and AY for always.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to renounce or deny.

clue.text: Seeds we scattered with genera, source of all higher plants (13, two words)

indicators.note: scattered means the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Seeds scattered among genera, the origin of all advanced plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges SEEDS WE together with GENERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Green algae are thought to be the ancestors of all land plants.
